newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Customs to take over Schiphol cargo centre.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Customs to take over Schiphol cargo centre.

text.p: Amsterdam Schiphol airport's cargo centre is to be formally taken over by Dutch Customs following an agreement signed on Monday, an airport statement said.
The move forces the majority of the local cargo community to move to other parts of the airport as all customs services will now be brought under one roof.
All of the customs facilities will be based in the building from December 31, 1998. They will be available 24 hours a day.
Cargo Centre Schiphol, built in 1967, lies at the heart of the Dutch air cargo industry.
The building is 8,100 square metres. Dutch customs will rent 7,400 sq m for a period of five years. As well as customs, Cargonaut will remain in the building.
Benefits for the customers include the fact Cargonaut, the automated freight transaction system, and customs are now in one building, the statement noted
The deal is worth 2.5 million guilders a year to Schiphol, the statement added.
